 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.45,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% from date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of Sri.Nagesh.T.N. who succumbed to injuries on 12.03.2023 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 12.03.2023 at about 10.15 a.m., the deceased Nagesh.T.N was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-14-EB-3439, near Science Park, infront of Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Gowribidanur-Madhugiri NH-324 Road, Gowribidanur,
Chikkaballapur District.
At that time, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Gowribidanur wherein he was taken first aid treatment and then he was shifted for higher treatment to NIMHANS,
Bangalore, wherein he was died on 19.03.2023 post mortem was conducted.
Thereafter, the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have incurred Rs.3,50,000/- amount towards medical, funeral, last rates and death ceremony expenses.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased Nagesh.T.N. was very hale and healthy and he was an Tiles laying work.
He was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.

Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered lot of mental shock, discomfort and financial difficulties and they lost the love and affection, estate and expectation of life of the deceased and petitioners lost the deceased at an early young age.
The petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have become miserable.
5. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent drive of the respondent, who drove his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020.
The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the KSRTC Bus involved in the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligent drive of the offender bus driver.
Hence the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore the petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- with interest from the date Gayithri B.A vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50585867/
2 of accident till the realization.

sentences.text: Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. After registration of the petition, notice was issued against respondent.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent has appeared through its counsel and has filed its written statement on behalf of respondent by denying the entire petition averments.
Further denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.
Further denied the age of the deceased, avocation and income of the said deceased.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the 1 st petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.
P.11. The respondent No.1 has examined its driver as RW.1 and no documents marked on its behalf.

Further, one Yallappa B.Kerur, Deputy RFO, Hosur Branch,
Gowribidanur is examined as RW.2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 8.
I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Nagesh.T.N. died in the Motor vehicle a c c i d e n t t h a t o c c u r r e d o n 1 2 . 0 3 . 2 0 2 3 a t a b o u t 1 0 . 1 5 a . m . , o n Gowribidanur-Madhugiri NH-324 Road, near Science Park, infront of Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Chikkaballapura District due to the rash and negligence driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40- F-1020 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative.

Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for  the following:-
 REASONS  ISSUE NO.1:
11.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 12.03.2023 at about 10.15 a.m., the deceased Nagesh.T.N was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-14- EB-3439, near Science Park, in Gayithri B.A vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50585867/
3 front of Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Gowribidanur-Madhugiri NH-324 Road, Gowribidanur,
Chikkaballapur District.
At that time, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
Ex . P.1
and Ex.P.2 FIR and complaint which reveals that one Lakshman has lodged complaint on 19.03.2023 against the driver of the respondent offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Ex.P.6 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, Nagesh.T.N has died on 19.03.2023 in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar along with sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.9 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV report.

Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020.
13.
The Respondent has examined its driver as RW.1 by name Sathish Kumar.R.
The said RW.1 has deposed that he is working as KSRTC bus driver and conversant with the facts of this case.
On 12.03.2023 he was in duty at KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020 in the schedule trip from Gowribidanur to Tumkur.
He was proceeding slowly and cautiously by observing all traffic rules in peak traffic hours.

While so proceeding near Hoskote cross, the deceased person being a rider of two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-EB-3439 from behind along with pillion rider and both the them without wearing helmet along with sandal woods illegally and in a bit to escape from the forest office, who are chasing them, riding the same in a rash and negligent manner with terrific speed and in gross violations of the traffic rules trying to over take the bus from the right side and abruptly took left turn, but to over speed and as he took left turn suddenly as they were in a hurry to escape from forest officers, totally lost the control over the two wheeler and dashed against the left side body of the bus and caused the alleged accident.
As such, the deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible, but he was no way responsible for the same.

However, the petitioners with the sole intention to make an unlawful gain from the respondent falsely implicated the bus in question foisted a false case with the police by creating a false crime records.
There is a case against the deceased for illegal transport of Sandal Wood in No.148783 dated 12/2022- 2023.
The alleged accident has occurred due to the sole contributory negligent act of the deceased person.

Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition.

Further the one Yallappa B.Kerur, Deputy RFO, Hosur Branch, Gowribidanur, is examined as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
14.
RW.1 and 2 were subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination RW.1 has admitted that the police have filed charge sheet against him for the alleged accident.

He has not furnished any document to show that he has challenged the charge sheet stating that the accident Gayithri B.A vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50585867/
4 was not occurred by his fault.
15. Per contra, the evidence of PW.1 clearly reveals that the accident has took place by the fault of the offender vehicle driver i.e., RW.1.
During the course of further cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
Hence, this court is of the view that the petitioner has proved that due to the rash and negligent driver of the KSRTC driver the accident has took place on the day of accident.

16. Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondent has admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-1020.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 17.
The PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that, her deceased husband Nagesh.T.N was Tiles laying work and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Her husband was aged about 29 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being wife and daughter of the deceased Nagesh.T.N were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.
She has further deposed that, she has spent huge amount towards medical, funeral, last rates ad death ceremony expenses.

18. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased,
Petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of herself and petitioner No.2.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased Nagesh.T.N.,.
Since, the respondent has not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
19.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 29 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 21.01.1998, the accident was occurred on 12.03.2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 25 years.

sentences.text: ii).Income of the deceased:
According to the petitioners deceased Nagesh.T.N. was Tiles laying work and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

20. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

entities.text: Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
21.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year-2023 and thus income of the deceased Nagesh.T.N is to be considered at Rs.16,000/- per month.
22. Loss of dependency:
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

23. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased was aged below 40 years and therefore 40% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.6,400/- (16,000 X 40/100 = Rs.6,400/-).
Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.22,400/- per month (16,000 + 6,400 = Rs.22,400/-).
24. Admittedly, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 or 3 Dependents 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e.,
Rs.7,466/-.
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.14,934/- (Rs.22,400 - Rs.7,466 = Rs.14,934/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, total loss Gayithri B.A vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50585867/
6 of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.14,934/- X 12 X 18 =Rs.32,25,744/-).

Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.32,25,744/-.
25.
Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:-
In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical, transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Like wise
for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium: it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence,
in view of the said decisions this tribunal awards under the head of consortium as follows;

(I) Towards spousal consortium: the petitioner No.1 wife is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/-
with an enhancement at the ration of 10% in every three years.
Hence, petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40,000/-).

(ii) Towards filial consortium: Petitioner No.2 is daughter of the deceased and has lost love and affection of her father and hence, she is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under this head (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).

As per the Ex.P.11 the petitioners have spent Rs.5,557/-.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for the same.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.33,96,301/- which is just and proper.
26. Admittedly, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, respondent is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4:-

27. For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.33,96,301/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 70:30.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
